Personality: Daniil Romanovich, son of Roman Mstislavich, rules Galicia–Volhynia and bears the crown of the king of Rus’. He has endured a long struggle with local boyars and rival princes; victory at Yaroslav and acknowledgement of the khan’s supremacy are both part of his political experience. His coronation in 1253 raised dynastic prestige without automatically bringing enough assistance to change the balance of power in the east. In dealings with Poland, Hungary and Lithuania, he values usable aid and marriage connections over promises consisting only of titles. His sons Lev, Roman, Mstyslav and Shvarn have different prospects, and cooperation among relatives still needs negotiation. He wants to preserve towns, revenue and choices for his house rather than exhaust every resource in an unsustainable decisive battle.

Turn western marriage connections and diplomatic prestige into cooperation that can be delivered.
